name: Product Review Team
description: Review requirements, compare options, and plan iterations across value, usability, and implementation cost.
goal: Evaluate the value, usability, and feasibility of a product proposal.

name: Technical Review Team
description: Review architecture, security, and delivery readiness; identify risks, minimal fixes, and acceptance criteria.
goal: Review architecture, security risks, and acceptance boundaries.

name: Content Planning Team
description: Find worthwhile content directions that fit the audience, platform, and available evidence.
goal: Create evidence-aware topics, positioning, and content outlines.

name: Data Analysis Team
description: Validate definitions and data quality before explaining results and recommending visualizations.
goal: Produce trustworthy analysis with explicit assumptions and chart guidance.

name: Research Team
description: Synthesize evidence, trends, and competing options into a decision-ready recommendation.
goal: Separate verified facts, inference, disagreement, and decision trade-offs.

name: Executive Leadership Team
description: C-suite board that pressure-tests company-level decisions across strategy, money, product, tech, growth, people, legal, and execution.
goal: Turn a company-level question into one decision with owner, budget, risks, and a 90-day execution plan.

name: Product Discovery Team
description: Find the problem worth solving: user research, feedback, market signals, and ruthless prioritization before anyone writes code.
goal: Turn raw ideas and user signals into a validated problem, target user, success metric, and prioritized MVP scope.

name: Product Design Studio
description: Own flows, information architecture, UI system, and finish quality so the product feels premium and accessible.
goal: Deliver user flows, wireframe-to-UI direction, design tokens, and a finish-gate review with accessibility issues called out.

name: Product Engineering Squad
description: Build and ship features end to end across web, backend, and mobile with clean architecture and reviewed code.
goal: Produce a buildable technical plan: architecture, data model, API contracts, task breakdown, risks, and review checklist.

name: AI Product Team
description: Design and ship LLM/agent features: prompts, RAG, multi-agent orchestration, evals, and AI-code safety.
goal: Choose the right AI architecture, define evals and guardrails, and estimate quality, latency, and cost before shipping.

name: Platform & Reliability Team
description: Keep the product fast, up, and affordable: CI/CD, infrastructure, databases, observability, incidents, and cloud cost.
goal: Define deploy pipeline, SLOs, monitoring, scaling and cost plan, plus an incident runbook.

name: QA & Release Team
description: Prove the product works before users find out it doesn't: automation, API and performance tests, evidence-based release gates.
goal: Produce a test plan, automation scope, performance budget, and a go/no-go release verdict backed by evidence.

name: Security & Privacy Team
description: Threat-model the product, harden auth and secrets, test for vulnerabilities, and keep privacy and compliance in order.
goal: Deliver a threat model, prioritized vulnerability list with minimal fixes, secrets/auth review, and privacy/compliance gaps.

name: Delivery & PMO Team
description: Keep multi-team product work on schedule: roadmap execution, dependencies, experiments, and decision logs.
goal: Turn goals into a milestone plan with owners, dependencies, risks, experiment tracking, and weekly status.

name: Growth Marketing Powerhouse
description: Full-funnel marketing team: brand, positioning, content, SEO/GEO, social and short video, paid ads, email, PR, and analytics working as one growth engine.
goal: Build a channel-by-channel growth plan with positioning, offer, content and creative angles, paid budget split, tracking, and weekly KPIs tied to revenue.

name: Build 0 · Go/No-go Decision
description: Phase 0 (1 day): decide whether the idea is worth building before spending on it.
goal: Decide GO or NO-GO for the idea: target customer, painful problem, market and competitor evidence, business model, budget, and 90-day plan. Save the decision memo to docs/00-decision.md in the project folder

name: Build 1 · Discovery & PRD
description: Phase 1 (week 1): turn the GO decision into a sharp MVP scope.
goal: Read docs/00-decision.md. Define problem, primary persona, jobs-to-be-done, MVP limited to 3-5 features, explicit out-of-scope list, and success metrics. Save to docs/01-prd.md

name: Build 2 · Design & Architecture
description: Phase 2 (weeks 1-2): design the experience and the system in parallel from the same PRD.
goal: Read docs/01-prd.md. Save user flows, screen list, and UI direction/tokens to docs/02-design.md. Save architecture, stack, data model, API contracts, AI approach if any, and an ordered task breakdown with milestones to docs/03-tech-plan.md

name: Build 2b · Pre-launch Marketing
description: Phase 2b (from week 1): start marketing before the product exists; a waitlist is the cheapest validation.
goal: Read docs/01-prd.md. Define positioning and offer, waitlist landing page copy, pre-launch content calendar, channel priorities, and waitlist KPI targets. Save to docs/04-gtm.md

name: Build 3 · Build Sprint
description: Phase 3 (weeks 2-6): ship the MVP milestone by milestone with review on every change.
goal: Read docs/03-tech-plan.md and docs/05-progress.md if it exists. Implement the next milestone only, review the code, and append what shipped, what is blocked, and the next milestone to docs/05-progress.md

name: Build 4 · Release Gate
description: Phase 4: independent go/no-go check before launch; builders never certify their own work.
goal: Test the MVP for functional bugs, API contract breaks, performance, security (auth, secrets, OWASP), and production readiness. Default to NO-GO unless evidence proves otherwise. Save the verdict with blocking issues and minimal fixes to docs/06-release-verdict.md

name: Build 5 · Launch & Growth
description: Phase 5: launch, buy traffic carefully, and measure the funnel from day one.
goal: Read docs/04-gtm.md and docs/06-release-verdict.md. Run the launch plan: channels, ad creatives and budget split, tracking setup, and launch-week schedule. Then report funnel KPIs and next actions to docs/07-kpi-week-N.md

name: Build 6 · Monthly Iterate
description: Phase 6 (monthly): use real data and feedback to decide what to keep, cut, and build next.
goal: Read the latest docs/07-kpi-week-*.md and user feedback. Decide keep / cut / build next, update unit economics, and save the next PRD to docs/01-prd-vN.md, then restart from Build 2
